ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: A living phrase is a phrase the records describe as not caught in verbal explanation, a fixed reasoning track, thought, or deliberation.
EvidenceBody: One direct definition is contrastive: “Speech containing speech is called a dead phrase; speech without speech is called a living phrase.” Another says that a phrase which does not fall into verbal explanation, does not drop into a track of reasoning, does not enter thought, does not permit deliberation, changes a thousand and ten thousand ways, and meets opposition on eight sides is called a living phrase. Gulin Qingmao records another description: “As for its living: a net will not hold it, a call will not turn its head, the ancient sages do not arrange it, and to this day it has no place.” A recurrent instruction says, “Investigate the living phrase; do not investigate the dead phrase.” Blue Cliff Record says that recognition under a living phrase is never forgotten, whereas recognition under a dead phrase cannot save oneself. Records also ask “What is a living phrase?” and preserve different answers, including “obtained within death.” An intermediate category, “a phrase neither dead nor living,” also occurs. These are the records' descriptions and classifications; the entry does not infer a hidden force behind them.
